6.1 Exercises 6- Exercises on the isomorphism theorems (S) Question 6.1.1. Let G and H be groups, with θ ∶ G → H a homomorphism. Prove that Im(θ) ≤ H. Question 6.1.2. Suppose n ≥ 2. There exists a surjective homomorphism σ ∶ Sn → C2. Prove that Sn has a normal subgroup K such that Sn/K ≅ C2. [The function σ is called the signature function, and we will study it in detail.] Question 6.1.3. Suppose G is a group with H ≤ G and N ⊴ G. Let ϕ ∶ H → (HN )/N be the map given by ϕ(h) = hN . Prove that ϕ is a homomorphism (we used this fact in the proof of the Second Isomorphism Theorem). Question 6.1.4. Consider the group GL2(R) (the group of 2 × 2 invertible matrices), the group SL2(R) (the group of 2×2 invertible matrices with determinant equal to 1) and the group P = {M ∈ GL2(R) ∶ det(M ) > 0}. (a) Prove that P and SL2(R) are normal in GL2(R). (b) Give an intuitive description of the quotient groups GL2(R)/SL2(R) and P /SL2(R) and GL2(R)/P . (c) Prove that, GL2(R)/SL2(R) P /SL2(R) ≅ GL2(R)/P.

Hint. (Question 6.1.1) Use the Quick Subgroup Test! Hint. (Question 6.1.2) Use the signature function as the homomorphism in the First Isomorphism Theorem. Hint. (Question 6.1.3) Recall the definition of multiplcation in quotient groups: (h1N )(h2N ) = h1h2N . Now check the definition of a homomorphism. Hint. (Question 6.1.4) Recall from linear algebra that if A, B, C are n × n matrices, then det(ABC) = det(A) det(B) det(C) and from this of course we have that det(A−1) = det(A) −1 whenever A is invertible.
